basis: Inflammation is confined to reproductive tissue; plasmacytic infiltrates alone do not establish infection or an autoimmune mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: nonspecific endometrial inflammation does not establish an infectious or autoimmune disease.

basis: Cerebral dysfunction, diabetes and nephropathy define the syndrome; defining deafness qualifies without a prevalence estimate and occupies involved because primary is capped at three.

decisions.renal: primary: nephropathy is an explicit defining component; prioritize intrinsic kidney damage within the three-primary cap.
decisions.otologic: involved: deafness is a defining component, retained through the diagnostic-feature exception after the primary cap.

basis: Typical 4p deletion causes neurodevelopmental impairment; skeletal abnormalities occur in ~60-70%, congenital heart defects ~40-50%, and hearing impairment ~40%.

decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects approximately 40% of the predominant Wolf-Hirschhorn phenotype, supporting common auditory dysfunction.

basis: Pigmentary dermatosis explicitly classified under ADAR-related type 1 interferonopathy; supplied HPO assigns torsion dystonia a frequency of 30-79%.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: explicit type 1 interferonopathy ancestry supports an immune-mediated mechanism; this is not inferred from a gene alone.

basis: Congenital cerebellar maldevelopment defines the disease; structural distal thumb phalanx abnormalities are annotated frequent (30-79%). Oculomotor findings reflect neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal thumb phalanx malformation is direct skeletal involvement and is annotated frequent (30-79%); hypotonia alone would not qualify.

basis: Cobalamin-processing disorder causing isolated methylmalonic acidemia; persistent neurologic or renal damage in at least 30% is not established for this responsive subtype.

decisions.neurologic: none: subtype-specific evidence does not establish persistent neurologic damage in at least 30%; severe MMA phenotypes cannot supply that estimate.

basis: Inherited sialic acid biosynthesis disorder causes degenerative skeletal myopathy; hypothyroidism is separately diagnosed and cardiomyopathy occurs in only 1-4%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defective sialic acid biosynthesis is an inborn metabolic disorder, supported by the glycosylation-disorder ancestry; hypothyroidism is not the justification.

basis: Adrenal cortisol excess causes myopathy/bone loss (~50-80%) and skin atrophy/striae (~50-70%) in overt Cushing syndrome; hypertension is separately diagnosed. Subtype estimates are limited.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension (~70-85% in overt Cushing syndrome) is a separately diagnosed disease; common intrinsic cardiac or vascular injury is not established.

basis: Arterial disease, joint hypermobility (12/14) and inherited cutis laxa define ATS; cleft palate is annotated frequent (30-79%). Keratoconus occurs in 3/14; refractive errors alone lack tissue injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is a direct structural defect of the mouth and is annotated frequent (30-79%).
decisions.ocular: none: myopia (6/15) and astigmatism (5/15) alone do not establish ocular tissue injury; keratoconus affects 3/14 (~21%).
decisions.dermatologic: primary: inherited cutis laxa ancestry and characteristic skin laxity/hyperextensibility establish a defining cutaneous connective-tissue disorder.

basis: Mitochondrial myopathy defines ophthalmoplegia and ptosis; cardiac abnormalities in one assessed patient do not establish >=30% prevalence. CNS and hepatic findings are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.cardiovascular: none: conduction abnormalities and ventricular bigeminy in 1/1 assessed patient establish possibility, but insufficient evidence of involvement in at least 30% of patients.
